purpose.summary: Confine every functional-test cache to its disposable scenario root and revalidate both public source identities before emitting legacy-compatibility evidence.
scope: Pass one explicit cache directory below each scenario execution root so inherited cached-chain fixtures never write into either governed source tree or share cache state across scenarios.
Launch every functional-test interpreter with bytecode writes disabled and verify the exact clean baseline and candidate source identities again after all four scenarios.
Preserve the exact build roles, scenario IDs, functional-test selection, compatibility oracles, sanitized report schema, and fail-closed cleanup law.
exclusions: No production-node, consensus, validation, P2P, storage, RPC, wallet, Chronik, activation, testnet, or mainnet change.
No scenario, build-role, inherited-test-selection, lifecycle-oracle, report-schema, or evidence-status change.
No incoming evidence, generated file, private source, private history, operator material, host metadata, or binary.

limitations: The public report observes only the exact ERGON-CHANGE-0010 candidate and cannot promote any later code or operator binary.

The four passing scenarios establish a bounded synthetic short-chain regtest observation with cross-node synchronization, clean restart, full reindex, chainstate reindex, manual physical pruning, post-prune mining, and one default-protected valid-chain reorganization on both roles.

The reorganization oracle uses an isolated baseline generator and identical raw blocks: a three-block incumbent, a replacement parked at equal work and a one-block lead, then activation at a two-block lead. It does not exercise P2P reorganization propagation, variable depth, invalid branches or transactions, DAA boundaries, mempool conflicts, restart or crash in flight, or reorganization across pruned history.

The normalized report does not serialize raw logs, physical paths, per-role pruning measurements, or per-step reorganization measurements; those oracles are enforced by the exact signed scenario and are not independently recomputable from the report alone.
Binary digests and config.ini source/build bindings do not prove build causality, and the dependency profile is not locked.
Historical-chain replay, sustained operation, public-network peers, operator-binary equivalence, real-datadir parity, and mainnet coexistence remain untested.
This evidence has an assembled-component ceiling and is not an independent reproduction pack.
counterevidence: No contradiction was observed inside the four declared public oracles, including the bounded default-protected reorganization lifecycle.

The prior read-only cache-path failure is closed for this exact run: every scenario completed, both source identities remained unchanged, the disposable work root was removed, and the report was emitted only after those checks.

A bounded raw-block reorganization does not establish P2P propagation, variable-depth or adverse reorganization behavior, invalid-branch or invalid-transaction handling, DAA boundaries, mempool conflict handling, crash recovery, pruned-history recovery, public-network behavior, or mainnet coexistence.
Build causality, reproducible builds, independent reproduction, operator-binary parity, historical-chain and real-datadir parity, and sustained operation remain evidence gaps.
